question.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $j$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}-j{a}_{2} & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $j=2.$
